The hip thrust.Clearly explained

400 KG · 0 BUDDIES

▼

What do you do?

Model. A 175 cm, 80 kg person viewed from the side, with the upper back on the edge of a 43 cm flat bench and a 100 kg barbell at the hips. This is a static model: each position is calculated as though held still.

Muscles. Glute brightness follows the torque required at the hip; quadriceps brightness follows the torque at the knee. Hamstrings extend the hip and bend the knee, so they contribute when the force line passes in front of the knee. Their brightness reflects a minimum-effort distribution of force between muscles. These are not EMG readings: this is a simplified mechanical model.

The white bar. The weight you could lift with the selected foot position and force direction, relative to the maximum possible in this model. It uses approximate maximum muscle forces. At each point in the movement, the first muscle to reach its limit sets the load, and the weakest position determines the result.

Scope. Explore how forces act and how to change them. This model does not measure an individual person.
